# California Consumer Privacy Act (Cal. Civ. Code §1798.100 et seq.): scanner coverage map

<!-- generated by scripts/compliance-coverage.mjs from the framework file; do not edit by hand -->

This page lists every control the scanner evaluates for California Consumer Privacy Act (Cal. Civ. Code §1798.100 et seq.), taken from `scanner/src/posture/compliance-frameworks/ccpa.json`, the file the engine reads. It is regenerated from that file and checked for staleness, so it cannot disagree with what is assessed.

```bash
/compliance --walkthrough ccpa
/compliance --report ccpa
```

**4 controls** are evaluated: 3 with an automated mapping, 1 needing a person to attest. By how much a code scan can observe: 2 yes, 1 partial, 1 no.

**Scope.** SELECTIVE SUBSET. 4 of the CCPA/CPRA obligations, chosen because a code scanner can produce evidence for them. The statute is far broader; the majority of its duties (notice, consumer request handling, contracts, retention policy) are organisational and are NOT represented here. Absence of a control is not a statement of compliance.

| Control | Requirement | Observable in code | Evaluated from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `§1798.100` | Consumer right to know — businesses inform consumers about categories of personal info collected. | partial | `module:privacy-taint` |
| `§1798.105` | Right to delete — businesses comply with verified deletion requests. | no | a person attests |
| `§1798.150` | Civil action for security breach affecting personal information. | yes | `family:crypto-weak-cipher`, `family:crypto-tls-version`, `family:crypto-tls-no-verify` |
| `§1798.81.5` | Reasonable security procedures and practices. | yes | `family:auth-missing`, `family:authz`, `family:hardcoded-secret` |

## What this does not do

<!-- limits-verified: 2026-10-20 -->

- **It is a subset.** Only the controls above are evaluated. Everything else in the framework is outside what a code scan can observe and is not assessed here.
- **It is evidence, not an assessment.** A control reported as present means the mapped signals are clean on the last scan. It is not an attestation, a certification or a statement of compliance.
- **A control needing attestation is not evidenced.** Those controls are listed so the gap is visible, and they stay open until a person attests.
